_rationale: Every one of the twelve frozen scenarios is classified here. An applicable scenario has a declared workflow that both lanes execute; assertions the oracle cannot express are listed as omitted, per scenario, so the denominator never shrinks silently. An inapplicable scenario names the host-side mechanism the oracle structurally lacks. Neither class is a pass.

WB-S001.reason: single-writer lease and lease-epoch semantics are host-side; the oracle has no lease

WB-S002.reason: max_bytes bounding, explicit loss and content-addressed raw refs are host-side observation policy; the oracle returns whatever the driver returns

omitted.stale target fails before backend invoca: generation-scoped target rejection is a host precondition

omitted.virtual clock is deterministic: already declared engine-specific on the native lane; the oracle has no clock claim either

omitted.provider class is recorded: the oracle has a single provider class, oracle

omitted.raw and normalized records are linked: the oracle keeps one event stream, not raw plus normalized

omitted.default is deny: the permission half cannot run: Playwright exposes no permission-request event for WebKit; permissions are granted per context in advance

omitted.undeclared path is rejected: the fixture-tree allowlist is host policy

WB-S009.reason: checkpoint, lease release and handover are host session semantics; the oracle has no checkpoint

WB-S010.reason: Playwright exposes no web-process termination for WebKit (page.crash is Chromium/CDP only), and checkpoint restore and redacted export are host-side

WB-S011.reason: exercises the host comparison engine itself; no browser is opened

WB-S012.reason: exercises host input-integrity checks; no browser is opened
